primary_issue_categories: Transcription artifacts (ASR markers, low-confidence tags, missing punctuation)
Technical term capitalization & formatting (Node, Node.js, DevOps, JWT, versions)
Contractions & punctuation (let's, it'll, I'll) and run-on sentences
remediation_steps: Remove ASR confidence/bracket markers (e.g. patterns like "[low-conf: ...]", "[unk]", "[inaudible]") from visible transcript; if marker indicates low confidence keep a note/flag for manual verification. Specifically: strip the tag but add a QA flag for seg 4 for human check.

Collapse duplicate adjacent tokens resulting from false starts/stutters. Automated rule: replace occurrences matching regex \b(\w+)\s+\1\b with \1. Apply with a whitelist/exception list (e.g., "that that" may sometimes be valid) and log replacements for human review (prioritise segs 4, 6, 17).

Remove filler-word restarts and redundant repeats (e.g., patterns like "um by by", "by um by") by removing typical fillers (um, uh, mm) when adjacent to duplicates or sentence boundaries. Use regex to remove isolated filler tokens and dedupe surrounding words; flag any sentence where removing filler materially changes meaning.

Standardize technical terms and capitalization using a mapping table applied case-insensitively with word-boundary matching. Minimum mappings: "node" -> "Node.js" (general reference), "node 16" or "node16" -> "Node 16" or "Node.js 16" (choose one style consistently), "devops" -> "DevOps", "jwt" or "Jwt" -> "JWT", "dashboard mobile" -> "mobile dashboard" (reorder where context indicates). Log all automated replacements for review (apply to segs 21, 25, 27, 28).

Fix contractions and common missing-apostrophe errors with context-aware replacements: "lets" -> "let's", "itll"/"itll" -> "it'll", "ill" at sentence-start -> "I'll". Use regex like \b[Ii]ll\b -> "I'll" only when preceding/following tokens indicate contraction (e.g., presence of a verb after); otherwise flag for human verification (apply to segs 8, 24, 27, 28).

Insert or correct punctuation to break run-on sentences and clarify clause boundaries. Automated heuristics: add periods where there is a long clause with multiple commas and no terminal punctuation; but mark segments with ambiguity for manual editing. Prioritise segs 21 and 25 for manual punctation fixes.

Run a QA pass that 1) reports all automated changes (diff) and 2) highlights sentences where automated rules conflicted or multiple issue types overlapped. Use that report to perform a manual pass on the highest-risk segments.
Maintain a replacement log and add unit tests/regex tests for each mapping to prevent overcorrection (for example, avoid changing 'ill' meaning sick to "I'll").
Final read-through by an editor to ensure tone, meaning, and technical accuracy preserved — focus manual effort first on segments flagged during automated steps.
